interest: Preserves expunged Takao Saito Diet interpellation and shows how the Diet was marginalized, plus FBIS-based wartime US intelligence methods.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.032, spanning February 1, 1940, to August 16, 1944, comprising 106 pages and 38 documents) documents U.S. diplomatic reporting, intelligence memoranda, official speeches, and international press commentary on the proceedings, structural reorganization, and legislative functions of the Japanese Imperial Diet immediately prior to and during World War II. The collection traces the collapse of parliamentary opposition and the consolidation of an authoritarian wartime state, beginning with the political upheaval and eventual expulsion of representative Takao Saito following his February 1940 interpellation challenging Japan's China policy. Subsequent reporting documents the dissolution of conventional political parties and the reorganization of the legislature under the Imperial Rule Assistance framework, featuring major policy declarations by Premiers Fumimaro Konoye and Hideki Tojo and Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka defending the Tripartite Pact and expanding state control. Covering the 76th, 81st, 83rd, and 85th Diet sessions, the records monitor wartime mobilization laws, record budget appropriations, secret foreign policy deliberations regarding Southeast Asia, and U.S. and Allied intelligence assessments regarding Japanese political stability and military intentions toward the Soviet Union.
